A day in the life of a sales assistant
A sales assistant helps customers find the right product in the shop; a cashier takes the payment and gives the receipt. In most shops, the same person does both.
The day starts with opening the shop: the shelves are tidied, the labels are checked and the till is opened.
Greeting the customer with a smile, listening to what they're looking for and guiding them honestly are the heart of the job.
Products are scanned, payment is taken, change is counted out and given, and a receipt is issued for every sale.
Incoming products are taken into the stockroom and put on the shelves; those closest to their expiry date are placed at the front.
It's learned in the marketing and retail field of vocational high schools, through courses or on the job. With experience, you become a section supervisor and store manager.
